intro.text: You break into a mine gallery: timbered, railed, ore carts standing where the shift left them. A painted sign reads [[shaft_nine:CALDER DEEP, SHAFT NINE, LEVEL 40]]. There is no mine this deep. Coolant drums are stacked by a pump station, and a lift cage waits at the head of a shaft going further down, its cable taut, its call bell still wired.

options.text: Tip the ore carts onto the conveyor.

carts.text: The carts are full of rich, heavy ore, sorted by a hand that took pride in it. You tip them one by one onto the conveyor. The last cart has a lunch tin wedged under the ore. Inside is a sandwich, still soft.

coolant.text: The drums carry a spec number you know from your own tanks. Whoever stocked this level used the same supplier. {crew} siphons the good stuff and copies down the delivery date from the stencil. {crew} reads it twice, then reads it aloud. It is next month.

sludge.text: The first drums are good. The last have gone to black sludge that clogs the intake and chokes a pump on your coolant loop. {crew} flushes it with a great deal of language and saves what they can. The rest goes back in the drums, and the drums go back on the stack, chalked with a skull.

cage.text: The cage drops for a long minute, the bell ringing at every level. At the bottom, {crew} finds a charging bay with one cell still sealed in its crate and ore stacked like firewood. They ride back up grinning. The bell keeps ringing after the cage stops.

cable.text: The cage drops, the bell rings at every level, and then the bell stops. The cable goes slack. You winch up forty meters of it, cut clean, not frayed. {crew} does not answer on any channel. The call bell rings once more, from very far below.
